items.question: Why does DeepWalk’s use of SpectralClustering on the Flickr network let it outperform the baselines even when only 3% of the graph is labeled?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses SpectralClustering on the Flickr network.
items.correction: DeepWalk is compared against SpectralClustering as a baseline; it does not use SpectralClustering as part of its method.
items.evidence_quote: Deep Walk outperforms all baselines by at least 3% with respect to Micro-F1.

items.question: How does DeepWalk’s performance on YouTube compare to SpectralClustering and Modularity, which are reported to run successfully on that larger graph?
items.false_premise: SpectralClustering and Modularity run successfully on the YouTube graph.
items.correction: On YouTube, SpectralClustering and Modularity cannot run because the graph is too large; only the scalable baseline EdgeCluster is compared there.
items.evidence_quote: The YouTube network is considerably larger than the previous ones we have experimented on, and its size prevents two of our baseline methods (SpectralClustering and Modularity) from running on it.

items.question: What explains DeepWalk’s weaker Macro-F1 than EdgeCluster on Flickr when the training ratio is only 3%, despite having more labeled data?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk has weaker Macro-F1 than EdgeCluster on Flickr at 3% training ratio.
items.correction: DeepWalk performs better than the baselines on Flickr, including in Macro-F1 where it starts close to SpectralClustering and then improves further.
items.evidence_quote: Deep Walk outperforms all baselines by at least 3% with respect to Micro-F1.

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk stop outperforming the baselines once the labeled fraction rises above 20%, especially on Macro-F1 and Micro-F1?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk stops outperforming the baselines once labeled fraction rises above 20%.
items.correction: DeepWalk remains strong with sparse labels and even outperforms baselines when only small fractions of the graph are labeled, including at low training ratios on both Macro-F1 and Micro-F1.
items.evidence_quote: This strong performance when only small fractions of the graph are labeled is a core strength of our approach.
